scenes.summary: Dryline field footage establishes the consequence before the machinery: Velez Reservoir still holds water and the town purifier is mechanically intact, but its Tetherwell authorization is suspended. A locked status panel sits beside full storage tanks and ordinary residents ration what remains.
scenes.settingText: Velez community water plant — sunlit municipal treatment hardware, full storage tanks, intact purifier rack, Tetherwell authorization panel showing suspended access.

dialogueInline.speaker: Dryline Reporter
dialogueInline.text: Velez’s well isn’t dry. The purifier isn’t broken. Tetherwell says their account is.

scenes.summary: Inside the mobile Launch-Shop, Arvin inspects a hairline fracture in a ceramic thruster nozzle while Milo sets down a coil of copper and listens to the cooling metal. Their first attempt to reach the locked purifier depends on a nozzle neither of them trusts yet.
scenes.settingText: Mobile Launch-Shop tanker interior — maintained retro-industrial aerospace workshop, painted metal, organized tools and a cracked ceramic thruster nozzle on the central bench.

dialogueInline.speaker: Arvin
dialogueInline.text: The weld looks confident. The fracture disagrees.

dialogueInline.speaker: Milo
dialogueInline.text: I heard it click on cooldown.

dialogueInline.speaker: Arvin
dialogueInline.text: Good catch.

dialogueInline.speaker: Milo
dialogueInline.text: That’s it?

dialogueInline.speaker: Arvin
dialogueInline.text: Would you like a medal or a second nozzle?

dialogueInline.speaker: Milo
dialogueInline.text: Second nozzle. Medal later.

scenes.summary: Lucia arrives with the hard deadline from Esperanza and a decommissioned interceptor capacitor that can replace their failed ignition component. She puts the capacitor on the bench beside the cracked nozzle; the mission becomes concrete and immediate.
scenes.settingText: Mobile Launch-Shop storage bay opening into the workshop — labeled component crates, maintained racks and a decommissioned interceptor capacitor on a rolling bench.

dialogueInline.speaker: Lucia
dialogueInline.text: Esperanza has six hours before the storage tank drops below clinic reserve.

dialogueInline.speaker: Arvin
dialogueInline.text: And that capacitor?

dialogueInline.speaker: Lucia
dialogueInline.text: From a decommissioned interceptor. Paperwork says scrap.

dialogueInline.speaker: Milo
dialogueInline.text: Does the interceptor agree?

dialogueInline.speaker: Lucia
dialogueInline.text: It no longer has opinions.

scenes.summary: A restored Tetherwell training film explains why basin-wide coordination originally mattered: unmanaged pumping once drove the aquifer toward collapse, and synchronized wells, reservoirs and treatment plants prevented one user from exhausting another community’s future.
scenes.settingText: Tetherwell archival training film — clean historical basin diagrams, pump timing graphics and optimistic footage of coordinated municipal water infrastructure.

dialogueInline.speaker: Tetherwell Narrator
dialogueInline.text: Before coordinated pumping, the basin came within months of collapse.

dialogueInline.speaker: Tetherwell Narrator
dialogueInline.text: Tetherwell synchronized wells, reservoirs and treatment plants so one user’s draw could not empty another’s future.

scenes.summary: At the Launch-Shop command deck, Lucia traces one narrow orbital pass over Esperanza while Milo checks the purifier handshake and Arvin limits the mission to a single authorization window. The rocket only has to prove one thing: an independent route can safely wake one locked purifier.
scenes.settingText: Launch-Shop command deck — paper maps, three mismatched displays, analog-digital controls and a plotted eleven-minute pass over Esperanza.

dialogueInline.speaker: Lucia
dialogueInline.text: One launch. Eleven minutes over Esperanza.

dialogueInline.speaker: Milo
dialogueInline.text: Eleven minutes is enough?

dialogueInline.speaker: Arvin
dialogueInline.text: For the purifier, yes.

dialogueInline.speaker: Lucia
dialogueInline.text: Good. We’re not fixing the whole desert today.

dialogueInline.speaker: Arvin
dialogueInline.text: I only brought one rocket.

scenes.summary: From a Tethergrid interception suite, Cyrus recognizes the improvised trajectory crossing Esperanza’s inhabited corridor. He orders tracking without kinetic fire and redirects the team toward identifying Arvin rather than turning the town into collateral damage.
scenes.settingText: Tethergrid mobile interception suite on a high Mojave overlook — graphite technical interior, trajectory displays and restrained cyan/amber status light.

dialogueInline.speaker: Cyrus
dialogueInline.text: Esperanza is under the corridor. No kinetic fire until they clear it.

dialogueInline.speaker: Cyrus
dialogueInline.text: Track the launcher. I want the architect more than the wreckage.

scenes.summary: Back in the tanker, Milo seats the rebuilt nozzle while Arvin deliberately backs off the torque specification after seeing how the ceramic is loading. Lucia watches the clock rather than the hardware as the deadline tightens.
scenes.settingText: Mobile Launch-Shop workshop — rebuilt ceramic nozzle in a bench fixture, calibrated hand tools and mission clock visible from the open command partition.

dialogueInline.speaker: Milo
dialogueInline.text: One more turn?

dialogueInline.speaker: Arvin
dialogueInline.text: One less, actually.

dialogueInline.speaker: Milo
dialogueInline.text: You could have said that before I leaned on it.

dialogueInline.speaker: Arvin
dialogueInline.text: I enjoyed the suspense.

dialogueInline.speaker: Lucia
dialogueInline.text: Both of you, faster.

scenes.summary: Milo rebuilds a valve housing around an old mechanical spring while Arvin searches for the correct backup seal. The age of the hardware is not treated as decay; the old component is maintained, understood and still useful because Milo knows exactly how it fails.
scenes.settingText: Launch-Shop mechanical bench — maintained valve housing, spring, seal kit, calipers and clean organized small-parts trays.

dialogueInline.speaker: Arvin
dialogueInline.text: Backup seal?

dialogueInline.speaker: Milo
dialogueInline.text: Blue collar. Under your left elbow.

dialogueInline.speaker: Arvin
dialogueInline.text: Why is it under my elbow?

dialogueInline.speaker: Milo
dialogueInline.text: Because you keep stealing my bench.

dialogueInline.speaker: Arvin
dialogueInline.text: Fair.

scenes.summary: At an old communications field, Lucia identifies a maintenance band that can punch through Tetherwell’s blackout but would expose the Launch-Shop transmitter. Rather than choosing for Esperanza, the crew sends the town the risk and asks whether to use it.
scenes.settingText: Decommissioned Mojave communications field — maintained legacy dishes and towers against bright desert sky, portable Launch-Shop link equipment and a visible route to Esperanza.

dialogueInline.speaker: Lucia
dialogueInline.text: This band gets through the blackout.

dialogueInline.speaker: Milo
dialogueInline.text: And lights us up?

dialogueInline.speaker: Lucia
dialogueInline.text: Probably.

dialogueInline.speaker: Arvin
dialogueInline.text: Esperanza chooses whether we use it.

dialogueInline.speaker: Lucia
dialogueInline.text: I already sent the question.

scenes.summary: Esperanza’s reply arrives on the Launch-Shop tablet: the community authorizes purifier access only and explicitly withholds pump-control authority. Lucia reads the narrow permission back to the crew while Arvin loads only the approved key.
scenes.settingText: Launch-Shop exterior work platform beside the communications field — tablet with a concise local authorization, rocket hardware in the background and the town route plotted on paper.

dialogueInline.speaker: Lucia
dialogueInline.text: They said yes.

dialogueInline.speaker: Arvin
dialogueInline.text: Purifier only?

dialogueInline.speaker: Lucia
dialogueInline.text: Purifier only. No pump controls.

dialogueInline.speaker: Milo
dialogueInline.text: Specific.

dialogueInline.speaker: Arvin
dialogueInline.text: People usually are when we ask them.

scenes.summary: Cyrus confirms that Esperanza has issued a local maintenance authorization. He still intends to stop the unlicensed orbital link, but orders his team not to interfere with the municipal well controller itself.
scenes.settingText: Tethergrid ridge position — Cyrus with rangefinder and compact interception equipment overlooking the Launch-Shop route and Esperanza’s municipal infrastructure beyond.

dialogueInline.speaker: Cyrus
dialogueInline.text: They have local authorization.

dialogueInline.speaker: Cyrus
dialogueInline.text: Jam the uplink after launch. Do not touch the well controller.

scenes.summary: On the dry lakebed the crew conducts what looks at first like the launch, but Milo hears the feed line change pitch during ignition. He aborts the static fire before the injector fails. Flame rolls under the restrained vehicle and dies without liftoff.
scenes.settingText: Dry lakebed test position — Launch-Shop rocket restrained for static fire, feed lines instrumented, control cable running to a low portable console.

dialogueInline.speaker: Arvin
dialogueInline.text: Three—two—

dialogueInline.speaker: Milo
dialogueInline.text: Cut it.

dialogueInline.speaker: Arvin
dialogueInline.text: Why?

dialogueInline.speaker: Milo
dialogueInline.text: Feed line changed pitch.

dialogueInline.speaker: Lucia
dialogueInline.text: Cut.

scenes.summary: After the test site clears, Cyrus examines a charred injector fragment and the absence of a launch track. He correctly concludes that the crew aborted before catastrophic failure and predicts they will repair and retry before dawn.
scenes.settingText: Dry lakebed after the static fire — charred injector fragment, restrained-vehicle marks and Tethergrid field team working under hard desert light.

dialogueInline.speaker: Cyrus
dialogueInline.text: Injector fragment.

dialogueInline.speaker: Cyrus
dialogueInline.text: They aborted before it failed.

dialogueInline.speaker: Cyrus
dialogueInline.text: Move the intercept east. They’ll try again before dawn.

scenes.summary: Milo finds the hairline split beneath a feed-line clamp and sleeves it while Arvin holds the assembly steady while his RIGHT-HAND graft works a torque tool. The repair is specific, fast and based on what the aborted test taught them.
scenes.settingText: Mobile Launch-Shop tanker interior at night — feed-line assembly under task lights, sleeve stock, torque tool and the failed clamp laid out for inspection.

dialogueInline.speaker: Milo
dialogueInline.text: Found it. Hairline split under the clamp.

dialogueInline.speaker: Arvin
dialogueInline.text: Can you sleeve it?

dialogueInline.speaker: Milo
dialogueInline.text: Can you stop asking questions you know the answer to?

dialogueInline.speaker: Arvin
dialogueInline.text: No.

scenes.summary: Lucia sees two Tethergrid vehicles taking position on the south ridge while Milo finishes the repaired seal and Arvin closes the fuselage access panel. The crew has enough time only if nobody adds another experiment.
scenes.settingText: Launch-Shop final assembly area before dawn — rocket fuselage open at one service panel, south ridge visible through the bay opening, tools already being packed.

dialogueInline.speaker: Lucia
dialogueInline.text: Two vehicles on the south ridge.

dialogueInline.speaker: Milo
dialogueInline.text: How long?

dialogueInline.speaker: Lucia
dialogueInline.text: Long enough if nobody gets artistic.

dialogueInline.speaker: Arvin
dialogueInline.text: Milo?

dialogueInline.speaker: Milo
dialogueInline.text: Seal’s good. I resent the accusation.

scenes.summary: In the control trailer, Arvin refuses to call the final go himself. Milo reads feed, guidance and the locally issued Esperanza key; Lucia confirms the decoy path. Arvin gives Milo the launch decision because Milo owns the failure data that matters.
scenes.settingText: Launch-Shop control trailer — physical switches, paper checklist, three mismatched displays, locally issued Esperanza key loaded and rocket visible outside.

dialogueInline.speaker: Arvin
dialogueInline.text: Checklist.

dialogueInline.speaker: Milo
dialogueInline.text: Feed green. Guidance green. Esperanza key loaded.

dialogueInline.speaker: Lucia
dialogueInline.text: Decoy path is live.

dialogueInline.speaker: Arvin
dialogueInline.text: Then we go when Milo says.

dialogueInline.speaker: Milo
dialogueInline.text: You’re going to make this weird, aren’t you?

dialogueInline.speaker: Arvin
dialogueInline.text: Almost certainly.

scenes.summary: Cyrus reaches a parallel ridge position close enough to order Arvin to stand down over an open maintenance channel. Arvin does not debate him; he looks to Milo while Lucia counts the remaining clean seconds in the orbital window.
scenes.settingText: Opposing Mojave ridges before sunrise — Launch-Shop pad on one side, Cyrus’s restrained Tethergrid position on the other, clear inhabited geography beyond the corridor.

dialogueInline.speaker: Cyrus
dialogueInline.text: Arvin. Stand down.

dialogueInline.speaker: Arvin
dialogueInline.text: Milo?

dialogueInline.speaker: Milo
dialogueInline.text: Window’s still clean.

dialogueInline.speaker: Lucia
dialogueInline.text: For thirty-eight seconds.

dialogueInline.speaker: Arvin
dialogueInline.text: That’s our answer.

scenes.summary: The Launch-Shop rocket lifts cleanly from the lakebed on the single true launch of the issue. Milo tracks the repaired feed line, Lucia tracks Tethergrid pursuit, and Arvin watches the trajectory settle onto the narrow Esperanza pass.
scenes.settingText: Dry lakebed launch site at dawn — one clean Launch-Shop ascent, bright exhaust against the Mojave, control readouts secondary to the physical vehicle and clear sky.

dialogueInline.speaker: Milo
dialogueInline.text: She’s up.

dialogueInline.speaker: Lucia
dialogueInline.text: Don’t celebrate yet.

dialogueInline.speaker: Arvin
dialogueInline.text: I wasn’t.

dialogueInline.speaker: Milo
dialogueInline.text: You absolutely were.

scenes.summary: Dryline records the result at Esperanza: the unregistered relay authenticates the purifier for eleven minutes, pumps treated water into community storage and then disappears from the usable channel when Tethergrid closes the route. The stored water remains.
scenes.settingText: Esperanza purification plant — previously locked purifier rack awake, treated-water storage filling, local status readouts and ordinary operators confirming the result.

dialogueInline.speaker: Dryline Reporter
dialogueInline.text: At 04:17, an unregistered relay authenticated Esperanza’s purifier for eleven minutes.

dialogueInline.speaker: Dryline Reporter
dialogueInline.text: The town filled three days of drinking-water storage before Tethergrid closed the channel.

scenes.summary: Back in the Launch-Shop after sunrise, Milo and Arvin clean the test bench while Lucia pins the first incoming community request beside Esperanza’s completed authorization. Nobody treats one successful pass as victory; the evidence has changed the next engineering question.
scenes.settingText: Mobile Launch-Shop tanker interior after the launch — same maintained workbench, repaired tools being put away, Esperanza authorization marked complete and a new community request pinned beside it.

dialogueInline.speaker: Milo
dialogueInline.text: So. It works.

dialogueInline.speaker: Arvin
dialogueInline.text: Once.

dialogueInline.speaker: Lucia
dialogueInline.text: You two are going to ruin this, aren’t you?

dialogueInline.speaker: Arvin
dialogueInline.text: Tomorrow we make it repeatable.

dialogueInline.speaker: Milo
dialogueInline.text: Tomorrow?

dialogueInline.speaker: Lucia
dialogueInline.text: He said the quiet part out loud.

scenes.summary: The morning after Esperanza, the Launch-Shop receives more community requests than the surviving relay can serve before orbital decay. Lucia spreads the requests across the command table while Milo calculates that the one successful satellite can honestly reach only one more town.
scenes.settingText: Launch-Shop command table at morning — multiple paper and digital community requests, decaying orbital track, one remaining service window and the crew’s ordinary breakfast pushed aside.

dialogueInline.speaker: Lucia
dialogueInline.text: Four requests overnight.

dialogueInline.speaker: Milo
dialogueInline.text: Seven now.

dialogueInline.speaker: Arvin
dialogueInline.text: How many can the satellite reach before decay?

dialogueInline.speaker: Milo
dialogueInline.text: Two, if we lie to ourselves. One if we don’t.

dialogueInline.speaker: Lucia
dialogueInline.text: Then one satellite is not a network.

scenes.summary: At a collapsed but recoverable solar relay site, Milo finds several legacy timing modules whose clocks still hold calibration. Arvin takes the clocks rather than the tempting power hardware, deciding that the next system should move information across the ground before asking another rocket to do everything.
scenes.settingText: Decommissioned desert solar relay site — intact recoverable timing modules among maintained legacy hardware, bright panels and clean salvage procedure rather than wreckage aesthetics.

dialogueInline.speaker: Milo
dialogueInline.text: These relays still have clean clocks.

dialogueInline.speaker: Arvin
dialogueInline.text: That’s what we need.

dialogueInline.speaker: Lucia
dialogueInline.text: Not engines?

dialogueInline.speaker: Arvin
dialogueInline.text: I am trying something radical. Fewer engines.

dialogueInline.speaker: Milo
dialogueInline.text: Write down the date.

scenes.summary: The crew mounts the first ground relay on a ridge and sends a low-power maintenance packet to a second node. The second node receives it weakly but legibly, proving that part of the basin can be bridged without orbit at all.
scenes.settingText: Open Mojave ridge — compact Launch-Shop telemetry dish, rugged ground relay box, line-of-sight to a second distant node and clear surrounding community geography.

dialogueInline.speaker: Lucia
dialogueInline.text: First ground hop is live.

dialogueInline.speaker: Milo
dialogueInline.text: Second node hears it. Barely.

dialogueInline.speaker: Arvin
dialogueInline.text: Barely counts during testing.

dialogueInline.speaker: Milo
dialogueInline.text: You have changed.

dialogueInline.speaker: Arvin
dialogueInline.text: Do not get used to it.

scenes.summary: A Tetherwell documentary explains the legitimate systems problem the crew is now inheriting: shared aquifers can be damaged by individually reasonable commands made without basin-wide timing, pressure and reserve information.
scenes.settingText: Tetherwell institutional documentary — basin cross-section, synchronized pump timing, pressure curves and reserve graphics over clean municipal infrastructure.

dialogueInline.speaker: Tetherwell Narrator
dialogueInline.text: Shared aquifers fail when independent users act on incomplete information.

dialogueInline.speaker: Tetherwell Narrator
dialogueInline.text: Tetherwell coordinates timing, pressure and reserve so local decisions do not become regional shortages.

scenes.summary: At the workbench, Milo discovers that Esperanza and Red Mesa use incompatible controller generations. Instead of replacing either community’s functioning equipment, Arvin has him build a small translator board between the old maintenance buses.
scenes.settingText: Launch-Shop electronics bench — copper heat sink, pressure-valve controller, two visibly different legacy connector standards and a hand-built translator board.

dialogueInline.speaker: Milo
dialogueInline.text: Esperanza speaks 2048. Red Mesa still uses the old twelve-bit maintenance bus.

dialogueInline.speaker: Lucia
dialogueInline.text: English?

dialogueInline.speaker: Milo
dialogueInline.text: Their pumps hate each other.

dialogueInline.speaker: Arvin
dialogueInline.text: Build them a translator, not a new pump.

scenes.summary: The third ground node repeatedly resets whenever the adjacent municipal pump motor starts. Milo reproduces the failure, measures the surge and realizes the network has to survive local electrical conditions rather than asking communities to redesign working water plants around Launch-Shop equipment.
scenes.settingText: Community pump station and relay cabinet — operating pump starter, compact relay power buffer, oscilloscope trace and clear physical separation between municipal equipment and Launch-Shop add-on.

dialogueInline.speaker: Milo
dialogueInline.text: Node three drops every time the pump motor starts.

dialogueInline.speaker: Arvin
dialogueInline.text: Surge?

dialogueInline.speaker: Milo
dialogueInline.text: Like a hammer.

dialogueInline.speaker: Lucia
dialogueInline.text: Can we move it?

dialogueInline.speaker: Milo
dialogueInline.text: Can we move the pump?

dialogueInline.speaker: Lucia
dialogueInline.text: Point taken.

scenes.summary: Three community operators appear on mismatched voice and text channels with different needs and different willingness to share credentials. Red Mesa needs a two-hour pump window, Esperanza needs six hours of purification, and Coyote Wells refuses to expose its maintenance key. Milo designs a read-only node for Coyote rather than forcing uniform participation.
scenes.settingText: Launch-Shop command cabin linked to three distinct community controller views — mismatched but legible local interfaces, paper notes and no single standardized Tethergrid dashboard.

dialogueInline.speaker: Lucia
dialogueInline.text: Red Mesa wants two hours. Esperanza wants six. Coyote Wells won’t share its maintenance key.

dialogueInline.speaker: Milo
dialogueInline.text: Then Coyote gets a read-only node.

dialogueInline.speaker: Lucia
dialogueInline.text: That was fast.

dialogueInline.speaker: Milo
dialogueInline.text: I’m getting tired of rebuilding everything because people are different.

dialogueInline.speaker: Arvin
dialogueInline.text: Useful fatigue.

scenes.summary: Milo adapts an old hydraulic valve interface into a visible mechanical confirmation device so a local operator can see whether a remote request is merely advisory or capable of changing equipment state. Arvin deliberately keeps the mechanism understandable at the pump room.
scenes.settingText: Launch-Shop mechanical bench beside a community valve cabinet — spring, hydraulic cylinder, physical indicator flag and clearly labeled local/manual positions.

dialogueInline.speaker: Milo
dialogueInline.text: This valve predates me.

dialogueInline.speaker: Arvin
dialogueInline.text: By a lot.

dialogueInline.speaker: Milo
dialogueInline.text: I was going to say you.

dialogueInline.speaker: Arvin
dialogueInline.text: And you chose employment.

dialogueInline.speaker: Lucia
dialogueInline.text: Focus.

scenes.summary: At the old launch site, Cyrus ignores the scorched pad and follows a newly installed ground cable leaving the area. He realizes the crew’s meaningful work happened after the rocket left and orders his team to trace the connection rather than keep hunting launch debris.
scenes.settingText: Scorched but orderly former Launch-Shop pad — Tethergrid field team, one new shielded ground cable leaving the site toward a ridge, Cyrus studying the connection path.

dialogueInline.speaker: Cyrus
dialogueInline.text: Stop chasing the rocket.

dialogueInline.speaker: Cyrus
dialogueInline.text: This cable was installed after the launch.

dialogueInline.speaker: Cyrus
dialogueInline.text: Find where it goes.

scenes.summary: Dryline assembles a basin-wide field montage: volunteers mount small relay boxes at a clinic, a farm pump room and a municipal treatment shed; each site uses different legacy equipment, and each keeps its own local controls while exchanging only the information needed for handoff.
scenes.settingText: Dryline field montage across three Mojave communities — clinic utility wall, farm pump room and municipal treatment shed, each with distinct legacy hardware plus compact Launch-Shop relay modules.

dialogueInline.speaker: Dryline Reporter
dialogueInline.text: The homemade relay over Esperanza lasted eleven minutes.

dialogueInline.speaker: Dryline Reporter
dialogueInline.text: What followed did not: volunteers began linking local controllers across the basin with equipment Tethergrid never designed to talk to itself.

scenes.summary: The first three-node handoff fails without damaging any water equipment: Red Mesa accepts a request while Esperanza still considers the packet premature. Milo finds the clocks thirty-two seconds apart and blocks the command rather than forcing the test through.
scenes.settingText: Three-node Copper Lattice test — paired local clocks, packet trace across Red Mesa and Esperanza, clear failed handoff indicator with all pumps remaining under local safe state.

dialogueInline.speaker: Milo
dialogueInline.text: Red Mesa says go. Esperanza says not yet.

dialogueInline.speaker: Lucia
dialogueInline.text: Same packet.

dialogueInline.speaker: Arvin
dialogueInline.text: Different clocks.

dialogueInline.speaker: Milo
dialogueInline.text: Thirty-two seconds apart. That’s enough to open the wrong valve.

dialogueInline.speaker: Lucia
dialogueInline.text: So we don’t open it.

scenes.summary: At the workbench, Arvin sketches the obvious fix: one central clock that every node would obey. Before he can develop it further, Milo points out that whoever controls that clock would control the network’s truth. The crew abandons the elegant centralized solution.
scenes.settingText: Launch-Shop workbench — copper coil, timing modules, Arvin’s central-clock sketch crossed beside multiple local clocks and handwritten handoff rules.

dialogueInline.speaker: Arvin
dialogueInline.text: Central clock would fix it.

dialogueInline.speaker: Lucia
dialogueInline.text: That’s what I was about to say.

dialogueInline.speaker: Milo
dialogueInline.text: Then whoever owns the clock owns the network.

dialogueInline.speaker: Lucia
dialogueInline.text: I hate when he gets there first.

dialogueInline.speaker: Arvin
dialogueInline.text: So do I.

scenes.summary: Milo builds the alternative into a rugged enclosure: each node keeps local time, signs its handoff, and sends the handoff over two independent paths. The design accepts disagreement and delay instead of hiding them behind one master clock.
scenes.settingText: Launch-Shop fabrication area — rugged relay enclosure open on bench, dual path connectors, physical signed-handoff indicator and local timing module visible.

dialogueInline.speaker: Milo
dialogueInline.text: Local time, signed handoff, two paths.

dialogueInline.speaker: Arvin
dialogueInline.text: And when one path dies?

dialogueInline.speaker: Milo
dialogueInline.text: The other doesn’t ask permission.

dialogueInline.speaker: Lucia
dialogueInline.text: That I like.

scenes.summary: From a Tethergrid interceptor position, Cyrus watches maintenance traffic continue with no launch activity and understands that the rocket is no longer the organization. He identifies a ridge relay as a lawful target and orders it seized while explicitly leaving municipal equipment untouched.
scenes.settingText: Tethergrid field interceptor on a high ridge — Cyrus with rangefinder, network trace highlighting one unauthorized relay box and municipal infrastructure clearly separated from it.

dialogueInline.speaker: Cyrus
dialogueInline.text: They’re not launching.

dialogueInline.speaker: Cyrus
dialogueInline.text: They’re connecting.

dialogueInline.speaker: Cyrus
dialogueInline.text: Seize the ridge node. Leave the municipal gear.

scenes.summary: Cyrus’s team removes the ridge relay while Arvin, Lucia and Milo watch from the opposite canyon. Lucia starts to calculate a recovery route, but Milo shows that the remaining nodes already have a southern path. The crew chooses not to contest the seizure and tests the route-around instead.
scenes.settingText: Opposing canyon positions — Tethergrid team physically removing one compact relay, Launch-Shop crew observing from a safe ridge, alternate southern path marked on portable equipment.

dialogueInline.speaker: Cyrus
dialogueInline.text: This relay is unlicensed infrastructure.

dialogueInline.speaker: Lucia
dialogueInline.text: He practiced that.

dialogueInline.speaker: Milo
dialogueInline.text: Do we need it?

dialogueInline.speaker: Arvin
dialogueInline.text: No.

dialogueInline.speaker: Lucia
dialogueInline.text: Then let’s disappoint him.

scenes.summary: With the ground lattice working around the seized node, Lucia plots the remaining geography and finds a ninety-three-kilometer basin gap beyond line-of-sight range. The crew finally identifies the one job orbit still has: a bridge between two independent ground clusters.
scenes.settingText: Launch-Shop exterior platform at dusk — Lucia’s tablet and paper basin map showing ground hops, one clear ninety-three-kilometer gap and two functioning clusters.

dialogueInline.speaker: Lucia
dialogueInline.text: Ground hops cover forty kilometers. The basin gap is ninety-three.

dialogueInline.speaker: Milo
dialogueInline.text: So after all that, we still need a rocket.

dialogueInline.speaker: Arvin
dialogueInline.text: One.

dialogueInline.speaker: Lucia
dialogueInline.text: You sound offended.

dialogueInline.speaker: Arvin
dialogueInline.text: I was enjoying the quiet.

scenes.summary: Lucia brings a military-grade interceptor shell stripped of seeker and warhead. Instead of turning the relay into a weapon, the crew uses the casing as a passive protective housing that makes the orbital bridge harder to seize or damage during deployment.
scenes.settingText: Launch-Shop loading platform — inert interceptor shell opened to show no seeker and no warhead, compact bridge relay fitting inside as passive protective casing.

dialogueInline.speaker: Lucia
dialogueInline.text: Interceptor shell. No warhead, no seeker.

dialogueInline.speaker: Arvin
dialogueInline.text: What does it do?

dialogueInline.speaker: Lucia
dialogueInline.text: Makes the bridge harder to grab.

dialogueInline.speaker: Milo
dialogueInline.text: Can we say ‘grab-resistant’ on the parts list?

dialogueInline.speaker: Arvin
dialogueInline.text: Absolutely not.

scenes.summary: The crew packs four locally signed ground keys and the compact bridge relay into the launch payload. No master credential exists in the vehicle; losing the rocket cannot grant authority over the ground network.
scenes.settingText: Launch-Shop payload-prep bay — compact bridge relay, four distinct locally signed keys, inert protective shell and rocket payload fairing ready for closure.

dialogueInline.speaker: Milo
dialogueInline.text: Four ground keys, two routes, one bridge.

dialogueInline.speaker: Lucia
dialogueInline.text: And no master key.

dialogueInline.speaker: Arvin
dialogueInline.text: You say that like you’re checking for contraband.

dialogueInline.speaker: Lucia
dialogueInline.text: I am.

scenes.summary: The finished rocket rolls into position carrying a payload much smaller than the launch vehicle seems to deserve. Milo finishes the last continuity check while Arvin is pleased precisely because the orbital component is no longer the whole system.
scenes.settingText: Dry lakebed launch position at golden hour — finished Launch-Shop rocket, small sealed bridge payload, minimal crew and no excess weapon hardware.

dialogueInline.speaker: Milo
dialogueInline.text: Payload’s almost insultingly small.

dialogueInline.speaker: Arvin
dialogueInline.text: Good.

dialogueInline.speaker: Lucia
dialogueInline.text: Don’t start.

dialogueInline.speaker: Milo
dialogueInline.text: He loves saying that now.

scenes.summary: The bridge rocket launches once while Tethergrid vehicles close on the lakebed. The dramatic question is not whether the crew can build a rocket again; it is whether the small bridge can join the already functioning ground clusters before the route closes.
scenes.settingText: Dry lakebed at dusk — single clean launch of the Copper Lattice bridge vehicle, Tethergrid vehicles distant enough to preserve safe corridor geography.

dialogueInline.speaker: Milo
dialogueInline.text: Wind’s clean.

dialogueInline.speaker: Lucia
dialogueInline.text: Tethergrid?

dialogueInline.speaker: Milo
dialogueInline.text: Two minutes out.

dialogueInline.speaker: Arvin
dialogueInline.text: Plenty of time.

dialogueInline.speaker: Lucia
dialogueInline.text: That is not your line.

dialogueInline.speaker: Arvin
dialogueInline.text: I’m trying optimism.

scenes.summary: As Tethergrid reaches the abandoned pad, the Launch-Shop crew is already moving with the portable timing modules while the bridge climbs overhead. They leave bulky launch tools behind because the ground clocks and local nodes are now more important than the vehicle.
scenes.settingText: Post-launch lakebed and departing Launch-Shop vehicle — vapor trail overhead, Tethergrid arriving at the pad, portable timing modules being carried while expendable launch tools remain.

dialogueInline.speaker: Lucia
dialogueInline.text: They’re on the pad.

dialogueInline.speaker: Milo
dialogueInline.text: Bridge is already above them.

dialogueInline.speaker: Arvin
dialogueInline.text: Then leave the drills. Take the clocks.

dialogueInline.speaker: Milo
dialogueInline.text: Never thought I'd see you leave launch hardware behind.

scenes.summary: The Copper Lattice activates across the basin. Esperanza hands a signed packet to the ridge network, the orbital bridge carries it across the ninety-three-kilometer gap, and Red Mesa accepts it under its own local clock. Coyote Wells receives status only, exactly as requested.
scenes.settingText: Multi-location Copper Lattice activation — Esperanza local node, ridge relay, small orbital bridge, Red Mesa controller and Coyote Wells read-only display connected by a clear comprehensible route.

dialogueInline.speaker: Milo
dialogueInline.text: Esperanza to ridge. Ridge to bridge. Bridge to Red Mesa.

dialogueInline.speaker: Lucia
dialogueInline.text: Coyote Wells?

dialogueInline.speaker: Milo
dialogueInline.text: Read-only, like they asked.

dialogueInline.speaker: Arvin
dialogueInline.text: Again.

dialogueInline.speaker: Milo
dialogueInline.text: You just want to watch it.

dialogueInline.speaker: Arvin
dialogueInline.text: Yes.

scenes.summary: One ridge node disappears from the map after Tethergrid seizes it, but the packet path shifts south before anyone in Launch-Shop intervenes. Milo confirms the traffic arrived through the alternate route. For the first time the network survives a deliberate loss without asking Arvin what to do.
scenes.settingText: Launch-Shop network view paired with field image of a seized relay — one node dark, alternate southern path active, destination acknowledgment received without central override.

dialogueInline.speaker: Lucia
dialogueInline.text: Ridge node is gone.

dialogueInline.speaker: Milo
dialogueInline.text: No—it’s just gone from the map.

dialogueInline.speaker: Arvin
dialogueInline.text: Difference?

dialogueInline.speaker: Milo
dialogueInline.text: Traffic moved south before I touched anything.

dialogueInline.speaker: Lucia
dialogueInline.text: There it is.

dialogueInline.speaker: Milo
dialogueInline.text: There what is?

dialogueInline.speaker: Lucia
dialogueInline.text: Repeatable.

scenes.summary: At sunrise the next morning, new requests begin stacking across three mismatched Launch-Shop displays faster than the crew can sort them. Some towns request purifier windows, others pump authorization or repair access, and even one town submits competing priorities. The Copper Lattice works; now access itself needs rules.
scenes.settingText: Launch-Shop control cabin at sunrise — three mismatched displays, rapidly multiplying community requests, paper strips and the stable Copper Lattice route still visible beneath the queue.

dialogueInline.speaker: Milo
dialogueInline.text: Three new requests.

dialogueInline.speaker: Lucia
dialogueInline.text: Four.

dialogueInline.speaker: Milo
dialogueInline.text: That one came twice.

dialogueInline.speaker: Arvin
dialogueInline.text: Same town, different priorities.

dialogueInline.speaker: Lucia
dialogueInline.text: So tomorrow we need rules.

dialogueInline.speaker: Arvin
dialogueInline.text: Before another rocket.

dialogueInline.speaker: Milo
dialogueInline.text: Can tomorrow be after breakfast?

scenes.summary: Before dawn, Arvin and Milo weigh the Public Sky payload, the upper-stage hardware and the propellant they can actually carry. Milo suggests adding more fuel; Arvin makes him walk the mass ledger backward until the trap is obvious: every extra kilogram of propellant requires structure and still more propellant to lift it. They recover margin by redesigning a heavy mounting frame instead of pretending the vehicle can simply grow.
scenes.settingText: Launch-Shop exterior work deck — maintained tanker/flatbed structure, organized field hardware, hard Mojave sun and broad desert horizon.

dialogueInline.speaker: Milo
dialogueInline.text: I keep wanting the answer to be more fuel.

dialogueInline.speaker: Arvin
dialogueInline.text: More fuel has to lift more fuel. Then it has to lift the tank and structure that hold the fuel. The vehicle charges interest.

dialogueInline.speaker: Milo
dialogueInline.text: So we lose weight somewhere that is not doing useful work.

dialogueInline.speaker: Arvin
dialogueInline.text: Now you are designing a rocket.

dialogueInline.speaker: Milo
dialogueInline.text: Were you this cheerful when you taught Lucia?

dialogueInline.speaker: Arvin
dialogueInline.text: Lucia never asked permission to learn.

scenes.summary: On the exterior work deck, Lucia lays three route transparencies over a sunlit basin map while Arvin and Milo secure a compact antenna frame beside her. Lucia shows that two aggressive launches could reach far more locked communities, but the schedule would leave almost no margin for verification, local draw limits or safe aborts.
scenes.settingText: Launch-Shop exterior work deck — maintained tanker/flatbed structure, organized field hardware, hard Mojave sun and broad desert horizon.

dialogueInline.speaker: Lucia
dialogueInline.text: Every unused minute is somebody waiting on equipment that already works.

dialogueInline.speaker: Arvin
dialogueInline.text: And every bad authorization can empty a shared well that also already works.

dialogueInline.speaker: Lucia
dialogueInline.text: I am not arguing for careless. I am arguing that delay has a body count too.

dialogueInline.speaker: Milo
dialogueInline.text: Then the queue needs to count both kinds of harm.

dialogueInline.speaker: Arvin
dialogueInline.text: Exactly. Reach is not the same thing as service.

scenes.summary: Cyrus studies Launch-Shop's discarded stage hardware and tire tracks rather than a generic map. The rocket debris tells him what Launch-Shop will need next: a narrow class of bearings, telemetry connectors and clean pressure-rated hardware that cannot be fabricated in the field. He orders surveillance on likely salvage sources instead of searching the whole desert.
scenes.settingText: Tethergrid mobile command platform — immaculate graphite corporate hardware, brushed alloy, tactile/glass controls, restrained cyan/amber status light and Mojave terrain beyond.

dialogueInline.speaker: Cyrus
dialogueInline.text: Stop searching for the people. Search for the part they cannot make.

dialogueInline.speaker: Cyrus
dialogueInline.text: The frame is disposable. The bearing is not. Neither is that connector.

dialogueInline.speaker: Cyrus
dialogueInline.text: He will trade distance for certainty. Give him three places to choose from and watch all three.

scenes.summary: Long geometric rows of drought-resistant crops glow beneath efficient drip irrigation. A smiling agronomist checks a Tetherwell controller while animated statistics celebrate improved yield per allocated liter.
scenes.settingText: Tethergrid corporate-partnership film — immaculate agricultural infrastructure at golden hour.

dialogueInline.speaker: Tetherwell Narrator
dialogueInline.text: Tethergrid's high-efficiency agricultural partners produce more food with less water—protecting regional supply through another record drought.

scenes.summary: The crew lowers the rebuilt payload cradle into place while rationing their clean water. Fine desert grit has contaminated a guidance connector and a machined sealing face; the normal shop answer would be a thorough wash and clean-room handling, but the camp cannot spend drinking water that way. Arvin, Lucia and Milo improvise a dry cleaning and inspection sequence, accepting slower work and more rejects.
scenes.settingText: Mobile Launch-Shop tanker interior — maintained retro-industrial aerospace workshop, painted metal, tactile analog-digital instruments, organized tools, practical task lighting and controlled localized wear.

dialogueInline.speaker: Milo
dialogueInline.text: At a real shop we would wash this until it forgot the desert existed.

dialogueInline.speaker: Arvin
dialogueInline.text: At a real shop the technicians are not choosing between cleaning hardware and drinking tomorrow.

dialogueInline.speaker: Lucia
dialogueInline.text: You say that like you have made the other choice before.

dialogueInline.speaker: Arvin
dialogueInline.text: I have worked for organizations with enough water to waste and still found ways to waste people.

dialogueInline.speaker: Milo
dialogueInline.text: Dry clean, inspect, cap it. I can live with boring.

dialogueInline.speaker: Arvin
dialogueInline.text: Boring hardware reaches orbit.

scenes.summary: Inside a Tethergrid mobile interception platform, Cyrus reviews the open request traffic and the new allocation rules on a glass display. He stops on a genuine Tetherwell suspension at Glass Basin, where a municipal purifier has less than a day of reserve, then overlays the community's location with a clean interception corridor. Rather than invent a false emergency, he orders his team to route the real need where Launch-Shop will see it.
scenes.settingText: Tethergrid mobile interception platform — immaculate graphite corporate hardware, brushed alloy, tactile/glass controls, restrained cyan/amber status light, Mojave terrain beyond.

dialogueInline.speaker: Cyrus
dialogueInline.text: Do not fabricate a crisis. Use the one the board already created.

dialogueInline.speaker: Cyrus
dialogueInline.text: If they mean what they wrote, they'll hold the limit even now.

dialogueInline.speaker: Cyrus
dialogueInline.text: If they don't, Glass Basin will show me.

scenes.summary: A cold-side seal begins to leak during a ground check. Arvin aborts immediately and isolates the line rather than gambling on launch. The failure exposes a material-compatibility problem in a salvaged seal whose service history is unknown. They now need a replacement from a specific class of industrial hardware before Tethergrid closes the area.
scenes.settingText: Mojave field launch site — maintained hand-built aerospace hardware, compact support equipment, practical rigging, hard desert light and broad unobstructed sky.

dialogueInline.speaker: Arvin
dialogueInline.text: Abort. We learned enough.

dialogueInline.speaker: Milo
dialogueInline.text: It looked fine yesterday.

dialogueInline.speaker: Arvin
dialogueInline.text: Appearance is not service history.

dialogueInline.speaker: Lucia
dialogueInline.text: The replacement lives forty miles toward the people hunting us.

dialogueInline.speaker: Arvin
dialogueInline.text: Then the seal has chosen today's route.

scenes.summary: Milo traces the Glass Basin packet across an old municipal relay, a public maintenance archive and Tetherwell service records while Arvin works the radio stack and Lucia compares route timing. They confirm that the purifier failure and access suspension are genuine, but the emergency wrapper entered the public network through a Tethergrid backbone node rather than from Glass Basin's local controller.
scenes.settingText: Launch-Shop mobile control cabin — compact maintained retro-aerospace controls, analog gauges, physical switches, restrained digital readouts and bright Mojave light through the windows.

dialogueInline.speaker: Milo
dialogueInline.text: The emergency is theirs. The invitation is not.

dialogueInline.speaker: Lucia
dialogueInline.text: Which means somebody wants us to help and somebody else wants to choose how we arrive.

dialogueInline.speaker: Arvin
dialogueInline.text: Good distinction.

dialogueInline.speaker: Milo
dialogueInline.text: I would prefer distinctions that do not have interceptors attached.

dialogueInline.speaker: Lucia
dialogueInline.text: Those are less educational.

scenes.summary: The polished farm footage continues on one side while leaked pumping logs scroll on the other. Its uninterrupted premium allocation rises as three neighboring residential zones change from restricted to suspended.
scenes.settingText: The Dryline Report — split-screen analysis of leaked Tetherwell allocation records.

dialogueInline.speaker: Dryline Reporter
dialogueInline.text: The farm used more water during the emergency than all three locked communities combined. Its parent company sits on Tethergrid's board.

scenes.summary: Cyrus stands over a terrain model inside the interception platform while a technician places Glass Basin's actual municipal boundary beside the projected launch corridor. Cyrus orders the interceptor geometry moved farther from the settlement and forbids any kinetic action until the rocket clears the civilian footprint, even though the safer interception point gives Launch-Shop more time.
scenes.settingText: Tethergrid mobile interception platform — immaculate graphite corporate hardware, brushed alloy, tactile/glass controls, restrained cyan/amber status light, Mojave terrain beyond.

dialogueInline.speaker: Cyrus
dialogueInline.text: Move the intercept south.

dialogueInline.speaker: Cyrus
dialogueInline.text: The board asked for the satellite. It did not authorize me to turn a water emergency into a crater.

dialogueInline.speaker: Cyrus
dialogueInline.text: Let them reach the hard part of their own argument. I want to know whether they still believe it when belief costs them something.

scenes.summary: Milo and Arvin run a low-energy pressure and fit check on the replacement hardware while Lucia packs the workshop around them. The test is intentionally incomplete because a full-duration noisy test would expose their location. Milo wants one more run; Arvin must decide what uncertainty they can carry into flight and what uncertainty is unacceptable.
scenes.settingText: Mobile Launch-Shop tanker interior — maintained retro-industrial aerospace workshop, painted metal, tactile analog-digital instruments, organized tools, practical task lighting and controlled localized wear.

dialogueInline.speaker: Milo
dialogueInline.text: Another run and I can tell you whether that chatter is the seat or the mount.

dialogueInline.speaker: Lucia
dialogueInline.text: Another run and Cyrus gets another chance to tell us where we are.

dialogueInline.speaker: Arvin
dialogueInline.text: We do not need perfect knowledge. We need to know which unknown can kill the flight.

dialogueInline.speaker: Milo
dialogueInline.text: I hate that being hunted has become part of the test plan.

dialogueInline.speaker: Arvin
dialogueInline.text: So do I. Pack the instruments.

scenes.summary: On a limestone ridge above the launch site, Lucia lays out a decoy route that keeps the real ascent away from Glass Basin and gives Tethergrid less reason to fire near civilians. The safer geometry reaches fewer communities than her earlier plan, and she marks those lost opportunities on the map instead of pretending they do not matter.
scenes.settingText: Mojave limestone ridge — pale fractured stone, bright high-desert sun, long sightlines, sparse scrub and the launch corridor below.

dialogueInline.speaker: Lucia
dialogueInline.text: This route protects Glass Basin and costs us two other windows.

dialogueInline.speaker: Milo
dialogueInline.text: Yesterday you would have called those two windows non-negotiable.

dialogueInline.speaker: Lucia
dialogueInline.text: I still hate losing them.

dialogueInline.speaker: Arvin
dialogueInline.text: And?

dialogueInline.speaker: Lucia
dialogueInline.text: And reach is not service if the people underneath it did not choose the risk. Write that into the rule.

scenes.summary: Minutes before the first launch window, the crew sends Glass Basin a plain-language disclosure showing the suspected Tethergrid trap, the proposed draw cap, the retaliation risk and a choice to accept, defer or request another route. The reply channel goes dead under deliberate interference. Milo watches the countdown pass the point where they could still launch on an inferred yes, and nobody reaches for the ignition controls.
scenes.settingText: Launch-Shop mobile control cabin — compact maintained retro-aerospace controls, analog gauges, physical switches, restrained digital readouts and bright Mojave light through the windows.

dialogueInline.speaker: Milo
dialogueInline.text: We know they need it. We know what they would probably say.

dialogueInline.speaker: Arvin
dialogueInline.text: We don't launch on probably. We wait for them to answer.

dialogueInline.speaker: Lucia
dialogueInline.text: Let the window go.

dialogueInline.speaker: Milo
dialogueInline.text: That is twelve hours we cannot give back.

dialogueInline.speaker: Lucia
dialogueInline.text: Correct. And it is still their twelve hours to risk, not ours.

scenes.summary: After dark, a signed Glass Basin packet arrives through an independent Dryline relay assembled from three local maintenance keys. The community accepts the exposure, chooses a six-hour purifier window below the shared draw limit and explicitly rejects any wider pump authorization. Milo verifies each key while Arvin and Lucia read the same terms over his shoulders.
scenes.settingText: Launch-Shop mobile control cabin — compact maintained retro-aerospace controls, analog gauges, physical switches, restrained digital readouts and bright Mojave light through the windows.

dialogueInline.speaker: Milo
dialogueInline.text: Three signatures. Six hours. Purifier only. No agricultural draw.

dialogueInline.speaker: Lucia
dialogueInline.text: They chose less access than we could give them.

dialogueInline.speaker: Arvin
dialogueInline.text: Which is why it is access instead of rescue.

dialogueInline.speaker: Milo
dialogueInline.text: You have been waiting all day to say that.

dialogueInline.speaker: Arvin
dialogueInline.text: I had twelve hours to edit.

scenes.summary: At the field launch site, Milo runs the checklist from the center position while Arvin works feed pressure and Lucia manages the route and decoy timing. The arrangement is visibly different from earlier launches: Milo calls each hold point, Arvin answers to him on the propulsion system, and Lucia waits for his clearance before committing the route.
scenes.settingText: Mojave field launch site — maintained hand-built aerospace hardware, compact support equipment, practical rigging, hard desert light and broad unobstructed sky.

dialogueInline.speaker: Milo
dialogueInline.text: Pressure stable. Community keys valid. Draw cap loaded. Arv, you are green.

dialogueInline.speaker: Arvin
dialogueInline.text: That sounded distressingly authoritative.

dialogueInline.speaker: Milo
dialogueInline.text: You gave me the abort.

dialogueInline.speaker: Arvin
dialogueInline.text: I know. I am enjoying the consequences.

dialogueInline.speaker: Lucia
dialogueInline.text: Enjoy faster. Route opens in forty seconds.

scenes.summary: Inside the Tethergrid interception platform, Cyrus sees the signed community keys appear in the launch telemetry just as a board directive authorizes seizure of the satellite. He studies the quorum, the published cap and the local rollback, then moves the intercept point one final time so any debris will fall away from Glass Basin.
scenes.settingText: Tethergrid mobile interception platform — immaculate graphite corporate hardware, brushed alloy, tactile/glass controls, restrained cyan/amber status light, Mojave terrain beyond.

dialogueInline.speaker: Cyrus
dialogueInline.text: They put the users inside the control loop.

dialogueInline.speaker: Cyrus
dialogueInline.text: That is either naïve or inconveniently serious.

dialogueInline.speaker: Cyrus
dialogueInline.text: Intercept after civilian clear. I want the satellite, not an argument written in casualties.

scenes.summary: During the final prelaunch run, vibration walks through the frame and intermittently corrupts one telemetry channel even though the propulsion hardware remains healthy. Milo wants to chase the bad reading; Arvin distinguishes between a sensor problem and a vehicle problem. Lucia forces them to decide what information is essential before the launch window closes.
scenes.settingText: Mojave field launch site — maintained hand-built aerospace hardware, compact support equipment, practical rigging, hard desert light and broad unobstructed sky.

dialogueInline.speaker: Milo
dialogueInline.text: The channel is lying.

dialogueInline.speaker: Arvin
dialogueInline.text: Or the mount is shaking. Either way, the other measurements agree the vehicle is not.

dialogueInline.speaker: Lucia
dialogueInline.text: Can you fly without that answer?

dialogueInline.speaker: Arvin
dialogueInline.text: Yes. I dislike it. Those are different statements.

dialogueInline.speaker: Milo
dialogueInline.text: I am writing that on your grave.

dialogueInline.speaker: Arvin
dialogueInline.text: Use legible lettering.

scenes.summary: Tethergrid disables the satellite over empty desert, but Glass Basin's controller has already cached the six-hour authorization and every enrolled community receives the compromised-route warning. In the Launch-Shop cabin, Milo watches the orbital icon vanish while the Glass Basin purifier remains green under its locally enforced cap. Arvin quietly marks the lost satellite off the board instead of treating the mission as a failure.
scenes.settingText: Launch-Shop mobile control cabin — compact maintained retro-aerospace controls, analog gauges, physical switches, restrained digital readouts and bright Mojave light through the windows.

dialogueInline.speaker: Milo
dialogueInline.text: Satellite is gone.

dialogueInline.speaker: Lucia
dialogueInline.text: Glass Basin?

dialogueInline.speaker: Milo
dialogueInline.text: Purifier is still running. Six-hour token is local. Draw cap is holding.

dialogueInline.speaker: Arvin
dialogueInline.text: Then the machine knew when to stop needing us.

dialogueInline.speaker: Milo
dialogueInline.text: That may be the first thing we built today that feels bigger than a launch.

scenes.summary: Immediately after the attempt, Arvin orders the crew to strip only the sensors, flight computer, scarce bearings and clean hardware from the test setup. They leave recoverable steel behind because Tethergrid is closing. Milo hates abandoning material they could use; Lucia points out that mobility is now a design constraint on the entire Launch-Shop operation.
scenes.settingText: Launch-Shop exterior work deck — maintained tanker/flatbed structure, organized field hardware, hard Mojave sun and broad desert horizon.

dialogueInline.speaker: Arvin
dialogueInline.text: Sensors, computer, bearings, clean fittings. Leave the steel.

dialogueInline.speaker: Milo
dialogueInline.text: I can use the steel.

dialogueInline.speaker: Lucia
dialogueInline.text: You cannot use anything from a cell.

dialogueInline.speaker: Arvin
dialogueInline.text: I love you both. I would also love to finish the failure analysis alive.

dialogueInline.speaker: Milo
dialogueInline.text: Clear, human, still somehow a work order.

scenes.summary: At a temporary limestone work site, Arvin and Milo hang the new payload and avionics on a crude balance fixture and discover the center of gravity has shifted aft. The rocket is not merely heavier; its mass is in the wrong place. Lucia arrives with news that their preferred salvage yard is under surveillance, forcing them to solve stability with the parts already on hand.
scenes.settingText: Mojave limestone ridge — pale fractured stone, bright high-desert sun, long sightlines, sparse scrub and the launch corridor below.

dialogueInline.speaker: Milo
dialogueInline.text: Same weight. Different place. Suddenly it wants to fly backward.

dialogueInline.speaker: Arvin
dialogueInline.text: Weight tells you how hard gravity pulls. Placement tells you how the vehicle argues with the air.

dialogueInline.speaker: Lucia
dialogueInline.text: Your actuator yard is being watched.

dialogueInline.speaker: Milo
dialogueInline.text: So the battery moves.

dialogueInline.speaker: Arvin
dialogueInline.text: The battery moves. Every cable complains. The rocket survives.

scenes.summary: Milo rebuilds the event from cached controller logs while Arvin measures the damaged pump. The shared limit itself was correct; the design failed because a single local credential could defeat it without a second person seeing the change. Lucia pushes them to separate accountability from blame before the whole network panics.
scenes.settingText: Community wellhead and pump yard — maintained water hardware, sun-bleached concrete, shade structure, visible mechanical gauges, clear piping state and hard Mojave daylight.

dialogueInline.speaker: Lucia
dialogueInline.text: Skip the shame for now. What do we make impossible?

dialogueInline.speaker: Milo
dialogueInline.text: One person could make a basin decision from a maintenance screen.

dialogueInline.speaker: Arvin
dialogueInline.text: Not again. If one screen can change everybody's water, one screen has too much authority.

scenes.summary: Inside a Tethergrid mobile command platform, Cyrus examines a control-surface hinge and worn actuator bearing recovered from the crew's previous site. He recognizes that Launch-Shop can rebalance the vehicle but will still need control authority in thin, fast airflow. Instead of searching camps indiscriminately, Cyrus orders quiet surveillance on an aircraft boneyard and two agricultural yards that stock rugged actuators.
scenes.settingText: Tethergrid mobile command platform — immaculate graphite corporate hardware, brushed alloy, tactile/glass controls, restrained cyan/amber status light and Mojave terrain beyond.

dialogueInline.speaker: Cyrus
dialogueInline.text: He solved balance. Now he needs authority.

dialogueInline.speaker: Cyrus
dialogueInline.text: Camps move. Requirements do not.

dialogueInline.speaker: Cyrus
dialogueInline.text: Watch the parts.

scenes.summary: A technician examines a cracked pump casing beside a community controller running the Launch-Shop's open protocol. A draw-history graph shows the pump exceeding its safe window after a local operator removed the shared limit.
scenes.settingText: The Dryline Report — forensic field report at a damaged community wellhead.

dialogueInline.speaker: Dryline Reporter
dialogueInline.text: Open access did not create more water. Someone overrode the community limit, damaged this pump and shortened the neighboring wells' remaining season.

scenes.summary: Back at the wellhead, Lucia tells Arvin they must publish their own logs before Tethergrid frames the incident for them. Arvin worries that halting the affected node will leave families short of water tonight. Rhonda rejects the false choice: tell the community exactly what happened, show the remaining safe volume, and let them decide how to use it.
scenes.settingText: Community wellhead and pump yard — maintained water hardware, sun-bleached concrete, shade structure, visible mechanical gauges, clear piping state and hard Mojave daylight.

dialogueInline.speaker: Arvin
dialogueInline.text: If we suspend this node, people lose water tonight.

dialogueInline.speaker: Rhonda
dialogueInline.text: Give me the safe number. Give me what happens past it. Then let us decide.

dialogueInline.speaker: Lucia
dialogueInline.text: Fine. Put the choice on the board.

scenes.summary: A gusty dry-lake test exposes a new problem: the improvised control surfaces have enough movement at low speed but not enough useful authority once the vehicle is loaded and the wind shifts. Arvin aborts the planned launch. Milo is furious at losing the window until Arvin shows that a rocket can have a functioning actuator and still lack enough aerodynamic leverage.
scenes.settingText: Mojave field launch site — maintained hand-built aerospace hardware, compact support equipment, practical rigging, hard desert light and broad unobstructed sky.

dialogueInline.speaker: Milo
dialogueInline.text: It moves. Full travel. No binding.

dialogueInline.speaker: Arvin
dialogueInline.text: Movement is not authority.

dialogueInline.speaker: Milo
dialogueInline.text: That sentence feels designed to ruin my evening.

dialogueInline.speaker: Arvin
dialogueInline.text: The air will ruin more than your evening.

dialogueInline.speaker: Lucia
dialogueInline.text: We lose the window, not the vehicle. Move it.

scenes.summary: The crew scavenges a rugged position sensor, shielded cable and mechanical linkage from a decommissioned tracking array and nearby farm equipment rather than finding a magical rocket part. Milo combines durable agricultural hardware with a precise aerospace sensor, while Arvin worries about response lag and Lucia watches the road for Tethergrid patrols.
scenes.settingText: Decommissioned Mojave tracking-array service yard — old dish drives, maintenance sheds, adjacent agricultural actuator stock, hard sun and blowing dust.

dialogueInline.speaker: Milo
dialogueInline.text: The farm actuator has spent twenty years eating dust and ignoring complaints.

scenes.summary: The mobile cradle enters the sandstorm because it hides them from Tethergrid tracking, but concealment costs engineering margin. Grit abrades exposed surfaces, clogs cooling paths and reduces optical visibility. Arvin orders slower travel; Lucia accepts the delay because arriving with a damaged rocket is not arriving. Milo begins rotating sacrificial covers and filters from the moving support truck.
scenes.settingText: Mobile Sky-Piercer launch route inside a Mojave sandstorm — low visibility, disciplined vehicle lighting, secured hardware, blowing grit and intermittent amber desert light.

dialogueInline.speaker: Lucia
dialogueInline.text: The storm is hiding us.

dialogueInline.speaker: Arvin
dialogueInline.text: It is also sanding the vehicle.

dialogueInline.speaker: Milo
dialogueInline.text: Filter is loading. I have another.

dialogueInline.speaker: Lucia
dialogueInline.text: How much slower?

dialogueInline.speaker: Arvin
dialogueInline.text: Slow enough that we still have a rocket when Cyrus finds the road.

scenes.summary: At the Tethergrid service transfer point, Lucia intercepts Rhonda's transport by triggering a legitimate maintenance closure on the storm-damaged road and forcing the convoy into a low-speed inspection lane. When the vehicle stops, Lucia disables its external door lock and Rhonda opens the interior release herself. No nearby community becomes a battlefield.
scenes.settingText: Mojave service road and Tethergrid transport corridor — hard-packed desert road, sparse utility structures, long visibility and disciplined vehicle spacing.

dialogueInline.speaker: Lucia
dialogueInline.text: Door is yours.

dialogueInline.speaker: Rhonda
dialogueInline.text: About time.

dialogueInline.speaker: Lucia
dialogueInline.text: You had the harder half.

scenes.summary: Cyrus sees the detention transport drop off the network and immediately understands that the launch route and rescue route are the same operation. He takes an interceptor toward the mobile cradle but orders the remaining units to stay off community roads where the storm has reduced civilian visibility.
scenes.settingText: Tethergrid mobile command platform — immaculate graphite corporate hardware, brushed alloy, tactile/glass controls, restrained cyan/amber status light and Mojave terrain beyond.

dialogueInline.speaker: Cyrus
dialogueInline.text: They tied the rescue to the launch.

dialogueInline.speaker: Cyrus
dialogueInline.text: Keep the pursuit on the service corridor. No blind crossings through settlements.

scenes.summary: A steering actuator begins to bind after grit gets past a worn outer seal. Milo does not declare the whole system broken. He compares commanded position with actual position, isolates the mechanical drag, replaces the sacrificial seal and cleans the protected bearing. Arvin checks that the actuator still meets the control margin established in Trip Point.
scenes.settingText: Mobile Sky-Piercer launch route inside a Mojave sandstorm — low visibility, disciplined vehicle lighting, secured hardware, blowing grit and intermittent amber desert light.

dialogueInline.speaker: Milo
dialogueInline.text: Command is clean. Position is late. That is drag, not guidance.

dialogueInline.speaker: Arvin
dialogueInline.text: Fix the drag, then prove we still have authority.

dialogueInline.speaker: Milo
dialogueInline.text: I miss when sand was scenery.

dialogueInline.speaker: Lucia
dialogueInline.text: You have four minutes to become nostalgic.

dialogueInline.speaker: Milo
dialogueInline.text: Failed seal is coming with us. I want to know why it lost.

scenes.summary: At the launch site, Cyrus reaches Arvin before fueling is complete. He has the authority and personnel to impound the vehicle, but a board command arrives ordering immediate remote lockout of every nonpaying Tetherwell community during the emergency. The order would cut functioning pumps regardless of each basin's actual reserve state.
scenes.settingText: Mojave field launch site — maintained hand-built aerospace hardware, compact support equipment, practical rigging, hard desert light and broad unobstructed sky.

dialogueInline.speaker: Cyrus
dialogueInline.text: Stand down the vehicle.

dialogueInline.speaker: Arvin
dialogueInline.text: You can stop the launch. You still haven't answered the lockout.

dialogueInline.speaker: Cyrus
dialogueInline.text: The lockout is a separate order.

scenes.summary: Cyrus compares the board lockout command with live Public Sky basin data that shows compliant draw, intact reserves and local trip protection. He does not join Launch-Shop or forgive the illegal launch. He refuses to execute a blanket water shutoff that has no conservation basis and tells the board he will enforce flight safety separately from subscription collection.
scenes.settingText: Mojave field launch site — maintained hand-built aerospace hardware, compact support equipment, practical rigging, hard desert light and broad unobstructed sky.

dialogueInline.speaker: Cyrus
dialogueInline.text: I will enforce the corridor rules.

dialogueInline.speaker: Cyrus
dialogueInline.text: I will not enforce account lockouts as safety orders.

dialogueInline.speaker: Lucia
dialogueInline.text: There it is.

dialogueInline.speaker: Cyrus
dialogueInline.text: It still does not make your rocket legal.

scenes.summary: The board bypasses Cyrus and orders an automated kinetic intercept against the launch corridor. Cyrus blocks the firing authorization because storm-obscured tracking cannot guarantee a safe exclusion zone around the mobile site. His refusal protects public safety, not Launch-Shop allegiance, but it removes the immediate strike.
scenes.settingText: Tethergrid mobile command platform — immaculate graphite corporate hardware, brushed alloy, tactile/glass controls, restrained cyan/amber status light and Mojave terrain beyond.

dialogueInline.speaker: Cyrus
dialogueInline.text: Tracking confidence below release. Denied.

dialogueInline.speaker: Cyrus
dialogueInline.text: Find me a clean shot or stand down.

scenes.summary: During pressurization, one booster feed begins to oscillate. The crew does not chase it into catastrophe. Arvin isolates the suspect path and accepts an eight-percent performance loss; Lucia immediately recalculates what that does to reserve and abort options. Milo confirms the remaining feed is stable. The vehicle will fly with less margin or not fly at all.
scenes.settingText: Mojave field launch site — maintained hand-built aerospace hardware, compact support equipment, practical rigging, hard desert light and broad unobstructed sky.

dialogueInline.speaker: Arvin
dialogueInline.text: Isolate it. We are not negotiating with an oscillation.

dialogueInline.speaker: Milo
dialogueInline.text: Remaining feed is steady.

dialogueInline.speaker: Lucia
dialogueInline.text: We just spent eight percent of the performance margin.

dialogueInline.speaker: Arvin
dialogueInline.text: Then tell me whether the remaining mission still closes.

dialogueInline.speaker: Lucia
dialogueInline.text: Barely.

dialogueInline.speaker: Arvin
dialogueInline.text: Barely is a number. Heroic is not.

scenes.summary: Sky-Piercer launches through the sandstorm. The early control surfaces work hard in gusts; onboard inertial guidance carries the vehicle when external navigation becomes unreliable; ground telemetry blanks behind the storm and terrain, then returns. The heat shield flexes and sheds sacrificial surface material without losing tiles. Every major season problem appears briefly as a system doing its job under stress.
scenes.settingText: Mojave field launch site — maintained hand-built aerospace hardware, compact support equipment, practical rigging, hard desert light and broad unobstructed sky.

dialogueInline.speaker: Milo
dialogueInline.text: External fix disagrees.

dialogueInline.speaker: Lucia
dialogueInline.text: Guidance rejected it.

dialogueInline.speaker: Arvin
dialogueInline.text: Leave it rejected.

dialogueInline.speaker: Milo
dialogueInline.text: Telemetry is gone.

dialogueInline.speaker: Arvin
dialogueInline.text: Our view is gone. The vehicle still has a job.

dialogueInline.speaker: Lucia
dialogueInline.text: Signal in three... two...

dialogueInline.speaker: Milo
dialogueInline.text: There.

scenes.summary: Rhonda joins the community allocation board from the launch site only long enough to confirm her rotated authority is no longer special. Delegates in separate communities approve the first cross-basin schedule carried by the new bridge without asking Launch-Shop to choose winners.
scenes.settingText: Community water-coordination room — practical municipal tables, printed basin maps, physical ledgers, rugged radios, pump telemetry and ordinary maintained public infrastructure.

dialogueInline.speaker: Rhonda
dialogueInline.text: My key is one of six now.

dialogueInline.speaker: Arvin
dialogueInline.text: Good.

dialogueInline.speaker: Rhonda
dialogueInline.text: You are getting very comfortable with that word.

scenes.summary: Cyrus watches the new bridge appear on a Tethergrid basin map beside multiple ground loops, local trip modules and independent community keys. There is no command center to seize and no single uplink whose loss would restore Tetherwell's exclusive control. Tethergrid still exists, conservation still matters, and the monopoly no longer defines the only workable network.
scenes.settingText: Tethergrid mobile command platform — immaculate graphite corporate hardware, brushed alloy, tactile/glass controls, restrained cyan/amber status light and Mojave terrain beyond.

dialogueInline.speaker: Cyrus
dialogueInline.text: There is no center.

dialogueInline.speaker: Cyrus
dialogueInline.text: That was the objective.

scenes.summary: At sunrise, the crew stands beside the cooling mobile cradle eating whatever breakfast survived the drive. Milo inspects the failed steering seal; Arvin reviews the isolated booster data; Lucia cleans sand from her boots and asks who is sleeping first. Rhonda joins them. Their conversation is mostly ordinary, with the enormous launch treated as work that now has maintenance attached.
scenes.settingText: Mojave field launch site — maintained hand-built aerospace hardware, compact support equipment, practical rigging, hard desert light and broad unobstructed sky.

dialogueInline.speaker: Rhonda
dialogueInline.text: Has anyone slept?

dialogueInline.speaker: Lucia
dialogueInline.text: Define slept.

dialogueInline.speaker: Milo
dialogueInline.text: The seal failed from abrasion before the bearing did. I was right to bring it.

dialogueInline.speaker: Arvin
dialogueInline.text: You were right. I dislike the precedent.

dialogueInline.speaker: Lucia
dialogueInline.text: Milo sleeps first.

dialogueInline.speaker: Milo
dialogueInline.text: I withdraw my finding.

dialogueInline.speaker: Rhonda
dialogueInline.text: Too late. Science has spoken.

scenes.summary: In a quiet Tethergrid office, Cyrus formally separates basin-safety enforcement from account-status lockouts in the orders under his authority, knowing the board can challenge or reverse him. The institutional fight is not over, but stewardship and subscription collection are no longer treated as identical in his command chain.
scenes.settingText: Tethergrid mobile command platform — immaculate graphite corporate hardware, brushed alloy, tactile/glass controls, restrained cyan/amber status light and Mojave terrain beyond.

dialogueInline.speaker: Cyrus
dialogueInline.text: Safety limits remain. Account lockouts require separate authority.

dialogueInline.speaker: Cyrus
dialogueInline.text: Put my name on it.

scenes.summary: The season ends with Public Sky carrying useful traffic, but the final image belongs to Launch-Shop work rather than infrastructure governance. A maintenance message reports an intermittent relay problem; another community asks for a future launch window. Arvin listens while Milo rolls a battered replacement engine component onto the deck. Lucia sees a distant Tethergrid aircraft changing course. Nobody says they have won. They start a new problem list and move.
scenes.settingText: Launch-Shop exterior work deck — maintained tanker/flatbed structure, organized field hardware, hard Mojave sun and broad desert horizon.

dialogueInline.speaker: Milo
dialogueInline.text: I found our next problem.

dialogueInline.speaker: Arvin
dialogueInline.text: That is an engine part.

dialogueInline.speaker: Milo
dialogueInline.text: Exactly.

dialogueInline.speaker: Lucia
dialogueInline.text: Tethergrid is turning south. We move in nine.

dialogueInline.speaker: Rhonda
dialogueInline.text: Public Sky can handle tonight without us.

dialogueInline.speaker: Arvin
dialogueInline.text: Good. Milo, tie down your problem.
